title: The Efficacy and Safety of Dalfampridine on Cognition and Fatigue in People With Multiple Sclerosis: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authors: Halabi MH, Alromayan R, Almutairi M, Alasmari H, AlGhamdi MA, Makkawi S
abstract: BACKGROUND: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a chronic autoimmune disease affecting the central nervous system. People with MS frequently experience cognitive dysfunction and fatigue. Dalfampridine (DAL), a potassium channel blocker, is US Food and Drug Administration-approved for the treatment of walking impairment in people with MS. It may also enhance nerve conduction in regions associated with fatigue and cognitive dysfunction. This study aims to evaluate DAL's efficacy in improving these symptoms, as well as its safety profile, in people with MS. METHODS: A systematic search was conducted across MEDLINE, ScienceDirect, Scopus, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and Web of Science, covering all records from database inception through April 1, 2024. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing DAL with placebo in people with MS and reporting impaired cognition and fatigue were included. A random-effects model was used to calculate the risk ratio (RR), standardized mean difference (SMD), and mean difference (MD) with 95% CIs. RESULTS: Of 1329 studies identified, 13 RCTs involving a total of 827 people with MS were included. DAL demonstrated a significant improvement in cognitive symptoms (SMD = 0.21; 95% CI, 0.04-0.38; P = .01; I² = 6%). However, no significant difference was observed between DAL and placebo in reducing fatigue (MD = 3.70; 95% CI, -4.37 to 11.77;P = .37; I² = 19%). Safety measures were comparable, with no significant difference in adverse events (RR = 1.11; 95% CI, 0.99-1.25; P = .08; I² = 0%). CONCLUSIONS: People with MS receiving DAL demonstrated significant improvement in cognitive symptoms; however, further studies are warranted to validate and confirm this finding.

title: Prediction Models for Delayed Bleeding After Colorectal Endoscopic Submucosal Dissection: A Systematic Review and Critical Appraisal.
authors: Miao D, Hou Z, Ge Y, Qi H
abstract: BACKGROUND: Although many predictive models have been developed or validated for delayed bleeding after colorectal endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD), their methodological quality and clinical utility remain uncertain. We systematically reviewed and critically appraised all available predictive models for this outcome. METHODS: We searched five databases through March 2026 for observational studies that developed or validated prediction models or scoring systems for delayed bleeding after colorectal ESD in adults (≥18 years). Two reviewers independently extracted data and assessed risk of bias using PROBAST. RESULTS: Of 25,177 records screened, five studies reporting five predictive models were included. The incidence of delayed bleeding ranged from 2.9% to 9.9%. The most commonly used predictors were lesion location and lesion size. Discrimination in derivation cohorts ranged from 0.726 to 0.890, internal validation areas under the curve [AUCs] ranged from 0.739 to 0.870, and the externally validated model achieved an AUC of 0.634. All studies were judged to have a high risk of bias, mainly because of inadequate reporting in the predictor, outcome, and analysis domains, although most had low concerns regarding applicability. CONCLUSIONS: This systematic review identified five predictive models for delayed bleeding after colorectal ESD. Lesion location and size were the most frequently reported predictors. Discriminative performance varied across derivation and validation cohorts, with suboptimal external-validation results. All models had a high risk of bias per PROBAST (low concerns regarding applicability); therefore, their findings should be interpreted cautiously.

title: Access to clinical cancer genomics and precision oncology-based care in North America.
authors: Kumar P, Salawu A, Demichelis-Gómez R, Williams A, Harris AR, Jenkins-Lord BD, Mullangi S, Bajaj RA
abstract: Despite the scientific and technical capacity for precision oncology in North America (Canada, the United States, and Mexico), its implementation is deeply uneven across the region. Our narrative synthesis of precision oncology implementation found that delivery consistently fails at four operational steps: biomarker testing, molecular interpretation, reimbursement, and access to matched standard-of-care therapy or clinical trial. These failures arise along disparity axes that differ by country but converge on a single outcome: patients whose cancers harbor actionable biomarkers do not receive precision oncology-based care. We conclude that precision oncology must be treated as essential cancer-care infrastructure rather than an optional research-based service and propose a tri-national implementation agenda. Acting now is particularly urgent given the rapid emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) models trained on precision oncology-derived datasets, which risk entrenching existing inequities into clinical decision-making before implementation reform can catch up.

title: Breaking the degenerative triad: Microenvironment reprogramming biomaterials for intervertebral disc regeneration.
authors: Zhao X, Han X, Hu Z, Chen Y, Wang X, Liu Q, Hu X, Zhang Q
abstract: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) represents a leading cause of chronic low back pain worldwide, imposing considerable public health and socioeconomic burdens. Current clinical interventions remain largely palliative, unable to reverse the progressive pathological cascade. This cascade is driven by a core self-amplifying triad of oxidative stress, chronic inflammation, and nutrient deprivation within the unique avascular, high-load disc niche, and ultimately progresses to end-stage terminal phenotypes such as biomechanical failure and neurovascular ingrowth. Over recent years, biomaterial-based regenerative strategies have evolved from passive structural fillers toward multifunctional platforms capable of active microenvironmental reprogramming. This review provides a systematic, critical synthesis of state-of-the-art advances in the field, organized within a hierarchical framework spanning immunometabolic modulation of the degenerative niche and targeted delivery of cellular and molecular therapeutics with further elaboration of precision-stratified design and whole-disc tissue engineering. We critically appraise evidence maturity across different strategy classes and dissect disc-specific translational barriers, noting that most candidate platforms remain at preclinical validation stages. Building on this analysis, we outline priority research directions and realistic near-term translational milestones to guide rational development of next-generation regenerative platforms toward durable functional disc repair.

title: Recent advances in functionalized electrospun nanofibers for biomedical and therapeutic applications: A comprehensive review.
authors: Deshmukh K, Pandey M, Moulahoum H, Ghorbanizamani F, Kovářík T, Przekora-Kuśmierz A, Jena H, Vora M
abstract: Electrospun nanofibers (ESNFs) have become a major focus of modern research given their adaptable architecture, extensive interface, and distinctive physicochemical characteristics, making them appropriate for varied applications such as catalysis and environmental cleanup, drug delivery (DD), tissue engineering (TE), sensing, actuation, and various energy-related technologies. As a result, electrospinning (ES) has emerged as a versatile manufacturing technique, driving intensive efforts to engineer nanofibrous structures specifically for biomedical purposes. Functionalization of ESNFs can be achieved by embedding functional agents or altering surface chemistry to introduce specific functionalities. This review discusses the fabrication methods, optimization techniques, and broad biomedical applications of modified ESNFs, emphasizing their key properties, including biocompatibility, degradability, and safety profile. The article outlines various strategies for creating and modifying ESNFs, followed by a comprehensive analysis of their applications in tissue regeneration, DD, wound repair, antimicrobial therapy, cancer diagnostics and treatment, and biosensing. By critically evaluating recent advances, highlighting future directions, and addressing ongoing challenges about ES, this review underscores the transformative potential of functionalized ESNFs as efficient and adaptable biomaterials for biomedical technologies.

title: Spatial mechanopriming of multicellular interfaces drives cytoskeletal-to-nuclear remodeling to boost therapeutic efficacy of stem cells.
authors: Bayaraa O, Lee NH, Kim SH, Lee H, Li CJ, Fu X, Hyun J, Choi G
abstract: Engineering multicellular constructs through biophysical cues, independent of soluble biochemical factors, is a promising strategy to boost the therapeutic potential of stem cells for regenerative medicine. However, the mechanisms by which spatially organized cell-cell and cell-matrix interfaces govern multicellular signaling and subsequent behavioral outcomes remain poorly understood. Here, we elucidate these mechanistic events by introducing 2D nanoplates (∼350 nm) compartmentalized within the intercellular space of mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) spheroids to form de novo cell-matrix spatial interfaces. These interfaces redistribute internal stress across the spheroid, amplifying integrin-cytoskeleton-nucleus force transmission and restoring YAP-dependent mechanotransduction to achieve spatial mechanopriming. Cells within these mechanoprimed spheroids exhibit profound nuclear deformation, epigenetic remodeling, and spatially patterned metabolic activation. Finite element modeling and spatial transcriptomic analyses further reveal a spheroid-wide reorganization of cytoskeletal and transcriptional networks. Mechanistically, elevated cytoskeletal tension across the reorganized interfaces is associated with a putative, tension-associated pseudo-hypoxic signature involving HIF-1α-related signaling, establishing a mechanometabolic niche that robustly enhances angiogenic secretion. Consequently, mechanoprimed spheroids demonstrate superior engraftment, accelerated vascular regeneration, and improved perfusion recovery in a murine ischemia model. Collectively, this work establishes spatial mechanopriming as an effective strategy to remodel cytoskeletal-to-nuclear mechanics and enhance the therapeutic potential of 3D multicellular systems.

title: A dithioacetal-based NIR fluorescent chemosensor for Hg2+ detection in biological and environmental samples.
authors: Wan J, Li W, Chen M, Wang Y, Yang X, Zhu M
journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
abstract: The widespread occurrence, high toxicity, and bioaccumulative nature of mercury (Hg2+) render its pollution a critical concern for ecosystems and human well-being. Hence, a novel near-infrared (NIR) fluorescent chemosensor (DHDM) was constructed through a naphthyl-substituted dicyanoisophorone dye and a 1,2-ethanedithiol recognition unit, which responds via a Hg2+-induced specific cleavage reaction and an ICT mechanism. DHDM exhibits excellent analytical performance, including a large stokes shift (192 nm), ultrafast reaction time (<1 min), sensitive detection limit (0.93 μg/L), which is significantly lower than the requirements of the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency's drinking water guideline standards. DHDM also exhibits high selectivity and robust anti-interference capability when challenged with various competing metal ions and amino acids. Such performance originates from the Hg2+-promoted deprotection of the dithioacetal moiety, which reinstates the conjugated fluorophore. The proposed reaction pathway has been corroborated by 1H NMR, HRMS, and DFT calculations. Meanwhile, DHDM successfully enabled in situ imaging of Hg2+ in HeLa cells, zebrafish, and germinating plant seeds, demonstrating good biocompatibility and tissue penetration, and yielding reliable recovery rates (89-109%) in spiked environmental water samples. Overall, the study establishes a reliable tool for mercury monitoring and constructs a multifunctional molecular scaffold, providing new perspectives for the rational design of advanced fluorescent chemosensors to address various challenges in the environmental and biomedical fields.

title: Effects of auxiliary acceptors on two-photon absorption and intramolecular charge transfer of D1-D-Ai-π-A hydrazone derivatives.
authors: Wang W, Chen M
journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
abstract: Hydrazone derivatives have recently emerged as promising candidates for two-photon absorption (TPA) materials due to their tunable donor-acceptor architectures and excellent nonlinear optical responses. Herein, the one-photon absorption (OPA), TPA, and intramolecular charge transfer (ICT) of four novel D1-D-Ai-π-A hydrazone derivatives modified with a planar trithiophene moiety are calculated using density functional theory and the sum-over-states method to study the effects of auxiliary acceptors Ai on the absorption spectra and the corresponding photoinduced ICT mechanisms. The computational results show that the stronger electron-withdrawing Ai group exhibits a red-shifted OPA maximum but reduces OPA intensity due to enhanced orbital separation. For the TPA, the derivative with a moderate electron-withdrawing Ai exhibits the largest cross-section, as it maintains balanced electron delocalization and efficient two-step charge reorganization, whereas an excessively strong electron-withdrawing acceptor induces localized charge recombination that suppresses TPA efficiency. The ICT analysis reveals that although strong electron-withdrawing acceptors enlarge electron-hole separation, overly strong withdrawal hinders long-range transfer. This work provides a design guideline for developing high-performance optical limiting materials based on hydrazone derivatives, and the underlying principle may offer useful insight for the design of other donor-π-acceptor systems.

title: Intelligent identification technology of zidovudine and its isomers based on active low-frequency terahertz excitation.
authors: Lu C, Pang S, Li Y, Su J, Tan K, Song Z, Tu S, Tang Y
journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
abstract: Zidovudine, adenosine, and vidarabine are three isomeric compounds with highly similar physicochemical properties, making them prone to confusion during pharmaceutical manufacturing, storage, and transportation. Therefore, the development of identification methods with high specificity and sensitivity for such isomeric compounds is of great significance for ensuring drug quality and clinical safety. However, conventional detection methods suffer from limitations such as high cost, long processing time, or insufficient resolution, rendering drug identification a challenging issue. This study introduces a non-destructive and intelligent detection method by integrating terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) with machine learning techniques. Transmission spectra of zidovudine, adenosine, and vidarabine were collected using a THz-TDS system and converted into absorbance spectra. Key features were extracted via t-distributed stochastic neighbor embedding (t-SNE), isometric mapping (Isomap), and principal component analysis (PCA). These were used to train support vector machine (SVM) and k-nearest neighbors (KNN) classifiers. Among the obtained models, the PCA-KNN combination achieved the most outstanding performance, with a classification accuracy of 100%, realizing precise discrimination of the three isomers. This method not only meets the quality control requirements of pharmaceutical standards and industrial production but also serves as a valuable reference for THz spectral detection of related drugs. It demonstrates promising potential for applications in precise drug identification and recognition.

title: Ortho-, meta- and para-substituted fluorescent probes based on BODIPY for detecting esterase with application in machine learning and bioimaging.
authors: Liu C, Liyang M, Bi Y, Wang Y, Zhang T, Sun B, Guo H, Li X
journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
abstract: Esterase plays a significant role in industrial production and life activities. The method of fluorescent probe is employed for detecting esterase due to their excellent performance. However, the restriction of recognition groups to specific positions severely limits the molecular design and performance optimization of fluorescent probe. Thus, three fluorescent probes (OBOD6, MBOD6 and PBOD6) based on BODIPY with recognition groups at ortho-, meta- and para- positions were designed and synthesized to systematically investigate the positional effects on performance of probes. All probes initially showed fluorescence quenching, followed by characteristic enhancement of fluorescent intensity at 587 nm (OBOD6), 577 nm (MBOD6) and 598 nm (PBOD6) upon esterase-catalyzed hydrolysis. Remarkably, OBOD6 exhibited the fastest reaction kinetics, nearly achieving conversion within 40 min at esterase of 0.6 U/mL. When incubated with esterase of 0.3 U/mL, MBOD6 (10 μM) nearly reached the reaction endpoint within 80 min, exhibiting the highest fluorescent enhancement and optimal detection sensitivity. MBOD6 could quantitatively detect esterase within a concentration range from 0.01 to 0.07 U/mL, with a detection limit of 2.23 × 10-4 U/mL. Besides, machine learning was additionally applied to the quantitative detection of esterase using MBOD6. The model explained approximately 93.19% of the variation in esterase concentration, indicating good overall fitting capability. Finally, leveraging its outstanding performance, MBOD6 was successfully applied to imaging of esterase in both cells and zebrafish.

title: Sustained delivery of 3D-bioprinted stem cell-derived small extracellular vesicles promotes neural regeneration following traumatic brain injury via the CREB1/PGC-1α/FNDC5 axis.
authors: Ai Y, Zhang Q, Chen T, Lin L, Chen Z, Liu G, Liu J, Dong Z
abstract: BACKGROUND: Clinical translation of stem cell-derived small extracellular vesicles (sEVs) for traumatic brain injury (TBI) is restricted by low yield in 2D culture and rapid in vivo clearance. OBJECTIVE: To develop an in situ sustained delivery system (3D-sEVs@Gel) encapsulating 3D-bioprinted adipose stem cell (ADSC)-derived sEVs (3D-ADSC-sEVs) within GelMA (Gelatin methacryloyl) hydrogel for long-term functional repair after TBI. METHODS: SEVs derived from coaxially bioprinted 3D-ADSCs were isolated, and a GelMA hydrogel-based delivery system was subsequently constructed. Following orthotopic transplantation of the 3D-sEVs@Gel system into the lesion site after TBI, functional recovery, neural stem cell (NSC) proliferation and lineage-associated responses, and the underlying molecular mechanisms were systematically evaluated through behavioral tests, immunofluorescence, multi-omics, and pharmacological inhibition. RESULTS: SEVs generated using the coaxial alginate-microfiber culture system exhibited an approximately eightfold higher yields and protein loading compared with those obtained from 2D culture. In vivo, 3D-sEVs@Gel prolonged local retention, reduced tissue loss, and significantly improved long-term sensorimotor coordination and spatial memory following TBI. In addition, treatment increased the numbers of proliferating cells co-expressing neural progenitor-, neuronal-, and oligodendroglial-lineage-associated markers within the examined neurogenic regions. Mechanistically, 3D-sEV treatment increased nuclear CREB1 levels in NSCs, promoting PGC-1α transcription and subsequent FNDC5 expression, thereby supporting endogenous neurogenesis and functional neural repair. CONCLUSION: The 3D-sEVs@Gel system promotes chronic neurological reconstruction post-TBI by modulating NSC proliferation and neural lineage-associated responses through the CREB1/PGC-1α/FNDC5 pathway, offering a promising cell-free strategy for neural repair and tissue engineering.

title: Spectroscopic and structural characterization of human amniotic membrane after washing with plasma-activated water.
authors: de Almeida FS, Calheiro GAT, do Nascimento JM, de Lima Cordeiro TB, Klausner V, Doria ACOC, Sant'Anna LB
journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
abstract: The human amniotic membrane (AM) is widely used in regenerative medicine; however, tissue processing and sterilization procedures may compromise its structural integrity. Plasma-activated water (PAW) has emerged as a potential alternative for tissue decontamination. This study evaluated the effects of PAW washing on the structural and molecular characteristics of human AM using histological and Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy analyses. AM fragments were divided into two groups: a PAW group, washed with plasma-activated water, and an antibiotic group (ATB), washed with penicillin, streptomycin, and amphotericin B. Following treatment, the fragments were cryopreserved and subsequently evaluated by histology and FTIR spectroscopy. Histological analysis revealed no apparent differences between the groups. FTIR analysis showed differences in band intensity in the amide III region on both membrane surfaces, while an additional difference at 1743 cm-1 was observed on the mesenchymal layer. Hierarchical cluster analysis (HCA) of the 1400-1700 cm-1 spectral region showed high similarity between the PAW and ATB groups. Principal component analysis (PCA) primarily separated samples according to membrane surface rather than treatment. Overall, PAW washing did not induce detectable histological or molecular alterations in human AM compared with conventional antibiotic washing.

title: Environmental Impact of Conventional Versus Underwater Endoscopic Mucosal Resection for Colorectal Lesions: A Procedure-Based Life Cycle Assessment With Pooled Effectiveness Estimates.
authors: Calabrese G, Moll F, Neves JAC, Bonacci L, Sinagra E, Castiglione F, Maida M, Albéniz-Arbizu E
abstract: OBJECTIVES: The environmental impact of endoscopic techniques remains poorly defined. We compared procedure-related environmental outcomes between conventional endoscopic mucosal resection (EMR) and underwater EMR (U-EMR) for colorectal lesions. METHODS: In this prospective pilot procedure-based life cycle assessment of the resection phase, 10-25-mm colorectal lesions underwent EMR or U-EMR across three endoscopy units. Outcomes included global warming potential (GWP, kg CO2-equivalent/procedure), waste, life-cycle water consumption, fossil resource scarcity, and terrestrial acidification. Exploratory GWP per en bloc resection was estimated using pooled randomized-trial and pilot-cohort data. RESULTS: Forty-nine procedures were included: 23 EMR and 26 U-EMR. En bloc resection was achieved in 56.5% of EMR and 69.2% of U-EMR, and R0 resection in 52.2% and 69.2%. Mean GWP was significantly lower with U-EMR than EMR (1.92 ± 0.54 vs. 2.42 ± 0.50 kg CO2-eq; p = 0.002), corresponding to a reduction of 0.50 kg CO2-eq per procedure and 50 kg CO2-eq per 100 procedures. U-EMR was associated with lower waste generation (324.0 ± 78.3 vs. 407.3 ± 72.0 g; p < 0.001), water consumption (0.56 ± 0.17 vs. 0.77 ± 0.20 m3; p < 0.001), fossil resource scarcity (0.33 ± 0.10 vs. 0.40 ± 0.09 kg oil-eq; p = 0.007), and terrestrial acidification (0.0052 ± 0.0018 vs. 0.0068 ± 0.0018 kg SO2-eq; p = 0.003). Findings were consistent across scenario and uncertainty analyses. In the meta-analysis-based model, GWP per en bloc resection was lower with U-EMR than EMR (2.59 vs. 3.51 kg CO2-eq), corresponding to a 26.3% relative reduction. CONCLUSIONS: U-EMR was associated with lower procedure-related environmental burden than conventional EMR, persisting after normalization for en bloc resection. TRIAL REGISTRATION: No. 165/26.

title: Feasibility of a Deep-Learning Model for Objective Visualization-Quality Assessment During Cholangioscopy-Guided Lithotripsy: A Proof-of-Concept Study.
authors: Kamada H, Kobayashi K, Yamana H, Fujita N, Namima D, Yamada M, Fujita S, Suto H
abstract: During peroral cholangioscopy-guided electrohydraulic lithotripsy (EHL), stone fragmentation obscures the visual field (the "snowstorm effect"), and visualization quality has been assessed only subjectively. This proof-of-concept study explored the feasibility of a deep-learning method for objectively quantifying visualization quality during EHL and, as an exploratory application, compared viscous gel immersion with saline irrigation. A ResNet-18 model was trained on expert-annotated frames (5-point scale) from three development cases. For independent validation, 120 frames from 12 previously unseen comparison cases were scored by two blinded endoscopists (inter-reader weighted κ = 0.98). The model showed only moderate agreement with their consensus (weighted κ = 0.60; accuracy 70.8%); because the validation sample was enriched for predicted-usable frames, metrics re-weighted to the natural frame distribution gave sensitivity 29.8% and specificity 93.5%, indicating systematic under-detection of usable views. Agreement did not differ systematically between gel and saline frames. The High-Quality View Rate (HQVR) was the proportion of EHL-phase frames scored Good/Excellent. In a patient-level comparison, median HQVR was 22.7% for gel versus 8.4% for saline (exact Mann-Whitney U, p = 0.15, not significant); in post hoc exploratory analyses, a threshold-independent mean predicted score differed (1.65 vs. 1.35, p = 0.005) and the longest continuous usable interval favored gel (median 24.4 vs. 5.2 s). Mild cholangitis occurred in 1/5 gel and 4/7 saline patients. Training such a model is feasible, but it is not yet a validated measurement tool, and the gel-versus-saline signal is hypothesis-generating only. Larger multi-case training and prospective validation are required. Trial Registration: N/A.

title: A benchmarking framework for organoid computing.
authors: Xing Y, Gao Y, Hong Z, Tian C, Cai H, Chu H, Yang Y, Liang PY
abstract: Organoid computing leverages functional neural networks of lab-grown neural organoids to recapitulate key aspects of human brain information processing, holding promising potential in brain-inspired computing, brain-computer interfaces, neuroscience, and medicine. However, its broad application remains constrained due to technical limitations including biological variability, interface instability, stochastic performance, and limited reproducibility. Here, we present a benchmarking framework that systematically quantifies the key performance determinants of organoid computing. We operationally define 'benchmark-ready' organoid substrates using optional criteria encompassing viability, cellular identity, structural integrity, functional maturation, and baseline networks, supported by multimodal phenotyping. We further establish qualification metrics for organoid-machine interface and intrinsic neural and network function, including physical coupling, spatial coverage, temporal stability, spontaneous activity, and network-level organization. Finally, we introduce a hierarchical evaluation framework for stimulation-evoked computation combined with information encoding criteria, standardized scoring, and statistical reporting. We believe that the benchmarking framework may provide an adaptable foundation for standardized, reproducible and comparable evaluation of organoid computing technologies, thereby facilitating the broad adoption and application of organoid intelligence.

title: Fabrication of carbon dots derived from Alangium salviifolium for the sequential sensing Ag+ and S2- and further monitoring of H2S in spoiled food.
authors: Qi X, Yang H, Xu D, Cui T, Dai Q, Chen G, Su Z, Chai F
journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
abstract: Given the significant threat posed by heavy metals to ecological system and human health, the development of precise, portable, and on-site analytical technologies is urgently required. Herein, multifunctional carbon dots (A-CDs) derived from the traditional chinese medicine (TCM) were synthesized and exhibited optimal emission at 604 nm excited at 495 nm, with quantum yield (QY) of 18.25%. The A-CDs achieved the cascade determination of Ag+ and S2- via a subsequent "on-off-on" process with LODs of 63.7 nM and 0.98 μM, respectively. Notably, A-CDs portable platform was constructed and enabled on-site quantitative analysis with LODs of 0.83 μM and 1.19 μM, respectively. Leveraging this unique sensing performance, the A-CDs test strips were developed for visual screening of H2S during food spoilage at varying storage temperatures, allowing qualitative food freshness discrimination via naked-eye observation. The precise quantitative detection in real water and foodstuff was applied, and further verified by ICP-MS, confirmed the excellent accuracy and environmental tolerance. This work presented an intelligent strategy for designing cost-effective, high-performance multivariate probes, holding significant promise for advancing food safety and environmental monitoring.

title: Lightweight interpretable support vector machine SERS (LiSVM-SERS) learning framework for serological diagnosis of psoriatic arthritis and biomarker identification.
authors: Zhang H, Lin W, Pan H, Cao L, Wang Y, Sun H, Zhao Y, Jia Y
journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
abstract: Psoriatic arthritis (PsA), a chronic, autoimmune form of arthritis that causes joint inflammation and occurs with the skin condition psoriasis, is difficult to clinically diagnose at an early stage due to insignificant symptoms and lack of biomarkers. Surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) is a powerful tool to identify specific biomolecules for liquid biopsy. Here, we establish a lightweight interpretable support vector machine SERS (LiSVM-SERS) learning framework for serological diagnosis of PsA and identification of potential biomarkers. The fs-laser-nanofabricated Au@mica SERS substrates with a relative standard deviation of 8.80% in intensity homogeneity are employed to obtain reliable serum Raman spectra. The SVM algorithm is performed to train the machine-learning model for PsA classification using only 26 samples (PsA = 13 and healthy controls = 13). The hyperplane coefficient vectors from the trained SVM model are then employed as the filtered weights of Raman shifts, followed by logistic-probability mapping and Welch's t-test to filter highly-significant spectral features, identifying 432 most-significant Raman shifts for 7 potential biomarkers. The trained LiSVM-SERS model demonstrates the outstanding sensitivity and specificity of 98.0% and 96.0%, respectively, validated by an internal independent blind-test cohort (PsA = 30, healthy controls = 30) and a cross disease-control cohort (systemic lupus erythematosus = 15, rheumatoid arthritis = 15, and osteoarthritis = 15). The present work not only provides a simple and lightweight non-invasive technique to diagnose PsA, but also paves a new way to identify the potential biomarkers from the label-free serum SERS spectra for autoimmune disorders.

title: Spatial organization of magnetic nanoparticles in chitosan-gelatin hydrogels enables enhanced magnetic actuation and cell response under dynamic stimulation.
authors: Viteri A, Ginebra MP, García-Torres J
abstract: Magnetically responsive hydrogels have emerged as promising platforms for remotely modulating HFF-1 fibroblasts behavior through dynamic mechanical stimulation; however, the influence of magnetic nanoparticle spatial organization on magnetic actuation and cell response remains unexplored. Herein, we report the development of chitosan-gelatin magnetic hydrogels with controlled Fe3O4 nanoparticle distribution including homogeneously dispersed, and spatially patterned configurations, as a strategy to engineer localized mechanotransduction and magnetic actuation. The role of nanoparticle organization on the physicochemical, magnetic, and biological properties of the hydrogels has been analyzed. Structural characterization confirmed the successful incorporation of Fe3O4 nanoparticles while preserving their crystalline inverse spinel structure. Morphological and topographical analyses revealed that patterned hydrogels exhibit well-defined nanoparticle-rich and nanoparticle-free regions, generating pronounced microscale heterogeneity throughout the material. The incorporation and spatial confinement of Fe3O4 nanoparticles significantly influenced the hydrogel properties, increasing stiffness, reducing swelling capacity, and enhancing magnetic responsiveness. Notably, patterned hydrogels displayed higher saturation magnetization and magnetic susceptibility than homogeneously dispersed systems, indicating that nanoparticle confinement promotes cooperative magnetic interactions and more efficient magnetic actuation. Biological studies demonstrated excellent cytocompatibility for all hydrogel formulations. While static magnetic stimulation slightly reduced fibroblast proliferation, dynamic magnetic stimulation significantly enhanced cell proliferation, spreading, and cytoskeletal organization, particularly in patterned hydrogels. These effects are attributed to cyclic mechanical cues generated by amplified magnetic-to-mechanical transduction within the patterned magnetic domains. Overall, this study demonstrates that nanoparticle spatial organization is a key design parameter for engineering magnetically responsive hydrogels with tunable magnetic actuation and controllable cellular responses for tissue engineering applications.

title: Irisin alleviates oxidative stress and osteoblast apoptosis in glucocorticoid-induced rat osteonecrosis of the femoral head via the integrin αVβ5/Bach1/Nrf2 signaling pathway.
authors: Zhang X, Zhang Y, Zhao Y, Song K, Liu X, Nan K, Fan L
abstract: Glucocorticoid (GC)‑induced osteonecrosis of the femoral head (ONFH) is associated with oxidative stress and osteoblast apoptosis. Irisin, the cleaved form of fibronectin type III domain‑containing protein 5, attenuates oxidative stress and apoptosis in numerous types of cells, including osteoblasts, osteocytes and cardiomyocytes. The present study aimed to investigate the role of irisin and the mechanism behind GC‑induced ONFH in vivo, as well as oxidative stress and osteoblast apoptosis in vitro. In the present study, GC‑induced ONFH was established in rats by intramuscular injection of methylprednisolone, with irisin administered by intraperitoneal injection; the FHs were then assessed by micro‑CT, histology, immunohistochemistry and TUNEL staining. In vitro, murine osteoblastic MC3T3‑E1 cells were treated with dexamethasone (DEX), and oxidative stress, apoptosis and Nrf2 signaling were evaluated by dihydroethidium/JC‑1 staining, flow cytometry, reverse transcription‑quantitative PCR and western blotting. Irisin prevented the development of GC‑induced ONFH in rats, and alleviated oxidative stress and apoptosis in DEX‑treated osteoblasts. To determine the underlying mechanisms by which irisin exerted beneficial effects on DEX‑treated osteoblasts, the present study investigated Nrf2 signaling cascades. Irisin induced Nrf2 signaling cascade activation in MC3T3‑E1 cells and Nrf2 silencing by targeted short hairpin RNA reversed the beneficial effects of irisin on DEX‑treated osteoblasts. Further mechanistic analysis revealed that irisin physically interacted with integrin (ITG) αVβ5 on osteoblasts, activating Erk1 signaling. This activation promoted nuclear export of Bach1, a competitive suppressor of Nrf2, thereby relieving Bach1‑mediated suppression of antioxidant response elements. Consequently, irisin enhanced Nrf2 nuclear accumulation and upregulated its target genes [heme oxygenase, NAD(P)H quinone oxidoreductase 1, glutamate‑cysteine ligase catalytic subunit], reducing reactive oxygen species and mitochondrial membrane potential loss. Pharmacological inhibition of ITG αVβ5 or Erk1/2 abolished irisin‑induced Bach1 export, Nrf2 activation and cytoprotective effects. Collectively, the present study indicated that irisin may mitigate GC‑induced ONFH and osteoblast apoptosis via the ITG αVβ5/Bach1/Nrf2 signaling pathway, highlighting its therapeutic potential.

title: Neurosurgical scalp incisions should preserve at least one vascular axis: Two case reports.
authors: Lupon E, Hertzog B, Njessi P, Camuzard O
abstract: BACKGROUND: Scalp necrosis after neurosurgery is usually attributed to repeated surgery. We report two cases in which necrosis was precipitated by a single reoperation incision that disregarded scalp arterial anatomy and the previous scars, and describe how this dictated the reconstruction. CASES: Case 1: a 56-year-old woman underwent emergency decompressive hemicraniectomy two days after meningioma resection, through a circumferential incision along the bone-flap margin that islanded the cutaneous flap from every axial pedicle; the whole hemiscalp necrosed with brain exposure. Case 2: a 15-year-old boy, operated on repeatedly for subdural empyema, underwent cranioplasty through an incision that transected the superficial temporal pedicle, the last axis supplying a scalp segment already isolated by previous incisions. In both cases the extent of necrosis and the absence of any remaining axial pedicle precluded local, regional or expanded flaps; a free latissimus dorsi muscle flap anastomosed to the superficial temporal vessels was the only option. Hair restoration in Case 2 was completed by follicular unit extraction onto the flap. CONCLUSIONS: A scalp flap survives only if at least one axial pedicle enters its base. Neurosurgical incisions, particularly at reoperation, should be drawn on the arterial map and previous scars; plastic and neurosurgical teams should share this rule.

title: Three-dimensional and dynamic assessment of digital lymphatic vessels using photoacoustic imaging.
authors: Suzuki Y, Uno T, Kajita H, Kato T, Takatsume Y, Imanishi N, Kishi K
abstract: Digital lymphatic anatomy has been defined largely by cadaveric studies. We evaluated whether photoacoustic lymphangiography (PAL) could depict three-dimensional anatomy and motion-related deformation in vivo. Two healthy volunteers and one patient with secondary upper-extremity lymphedema underwent fingertip indocyanine green injection, near-infrared fluorescence imaging, and static and dynamic PAL. In healthy fingers, lymphatic vessels coursed mainly along the lateral aspects toward the dorsal hand and lay between superficial veins and digital arteries. Flexion produced spiral-like deformation or abrupt angulation, whereas vessels were relatively straight during extension; segmental lymphatic signals moved proximally during motion. In the patient, PAL visualized vessels beneath dermal backflow that appeared more irregular and showed frequent short-segment tortuosity, and guided lymphaticovenular anastomosis. These findings support the feasibility of finger-specific, in vivo three-dimensional and motion-resolved assessment of digital lymphatic morphology using PAL.

title: CD36 promotes cholesterol gallstone formation by regulating cholesterol metabolism via SREBP2.
authors: Zhou H, Wang H, Ye X, Tan Y, Ruan S, Wang S, Yang W
abstract: BACKGROUND: Cholecystitis is a common biliary disorder, and cholesterol gallstones are a major underlying cause closely associated with disturbed cholesterol metabolism. However, the role of CD36, a multifunctional scavenger receptor, in cholesterol gallstone formation remains unclear. METHODS: Plasma proteomics was performed in patients with cholecystitis without gallstones (CC, n = 9) and cholesterol gallstones (GS, n = 63). CD36 levels in serum and bile were validated by ELISA and correlated with biliary lipid composition. In vivo, hepatocyte-enriched CD36 overexpression was induced by AAV8-TBG in lithogenic diet-fed mice, followed by assessment of gallstone formation, biliary crystal/sludge formation, gallbladder histology, serum and biliary lipid profiles, and cholesterol saturation index. In vitro, CD36 was overexpressed or knocked down in primary hepatocytes and HepG2 cells, and cholesterol secretion, protein expression, SREBP2 nuclear translocation, CD36-SREBP2 interaction, and rescue effects were analyzed using biochemical assays, Western blotting, co-immunoprecipitation, and re-expression/silencing experiments. RESULTS: CD36 was significantly upregulated in the plasma of patients with cholesterol gallstones and was further confirmed to be elevated in both serum and bile. Biliary CD36 levels correlated positively with biliary cholesterol and negatively with bile acid levels. In mice, hepatic CD36 overexpression exacerbated gallstone formation, increased serum lipids, elevated biliary cholesterol and cholesterol saturation index, and aggravated gallbladder injury. CD36 also increased hepatic expression of HMGCR, SREBP2, and PCSK9. In hepatocytes, CD36 promoted cholesterol secretion and upregulated these cholesterol metabolic regulators. Mechanistically, CD36 interacted with SREBP2 and enhanced its nuclear translocation. CONCLUSION: CD36 promotes cholesterol gallstone formation by enhancing SREBP2-dependent cholesterol metabolic dysregulation and may represent a potential therapeutic target for cholesterol gallstone disease.

title: Influence of cell seeding density and inoculation timing on HepG2 cell engraftment on the chick chorioallantoic membrane.
authors: Dehelean CA, Ali DH, Barna R, Predescu I, Macasoi I
abstract: Preclinical research on liver cancer requires models that closely mimic the biological environment, including three-dimensional tumor growth and vascularization, while ensuring rapid, inexpensive, and ethically favorable experimental conditions. Against this background, the chick embryo chorioallantoic membrane (CAM) offers a highly vascularized, immunologically immature (not yet immunocompetent) in ovo environment favorable for the engraftment of human tumor cells and in accordance with the 3R principles. HepG2 is the most widely used human hepatic tumor cell line, and although it is recognized as a malignant hepatic tumor, its precise classification remains debated. In this article, two cell densities (0.5 × 10⁶ and 1 × 10⁶ cells) were compared at three engraftment times (embryonic day 7, 8, and 9) to define reproducible engraftment conditions. Cohesive, histologically processable grafts were obtained only at the highest cell density, grafted on day 9, with a success rate of 85% (17/20 eggs). The five remaining conditions yielded no processable graft (0/100). Hematoxylin-eosin staining showed a cellular mass on the membrane, whereas the immunohistochemical panel (HepPar-1, Arginase-1, pan-cytokeratin) showed focal, heterogeneous staining. Therefore, the findings are compatible with a malignant hepatocellular tumor. The protocol is reported together with the five unsuccessful conditions as a practical reference for laboratories setting up the assay.•Cell density and grafting day determine cohesive HepG2 graft formation on the CAM.•Grafts formed only with 1 × 10⁶ cells on embryonic day 9 (17/20); others 0/100.•Five suboptimal conditions are reported as a CAM assay troubleshooting reference.

title: Trait-like proteomic signatures of stress resilience: correlates of freeze-like response resistance.
authors: Kučera J, Makarová M, Vít M, Novák J, Zlámal F, Ráčková L, Fialová Kučerová J, Grulichová M
abstract: The freeze-like response is a fundamental defensive mechanism that remains poorly understood despite its potential to impair functioning under acute threat. We examined its biological correlates using untargeted serum proteomics in participants exposed to ecologically valid simulated armed attacks, comparing untrained individuals (n = 20) with experienced police rapid response personnel (n = 20). Freeze-like responses, characterized by unresponsiveness to attack, were assessed via expert video analysis of participant performance during the scenarios. Serum samples collected before and after threat exposure were analyzed via LC‒MS/MS, identifying 1,238 protein groups. Experienced personnel demonstrated markedly greater resistance to freeze-like responses. No significant proteomic changes were observed from pre- to post-exposure in either group, suggesting that freeze-resistance may be associated with stable, trait-like signatures rather than acute stress-responsive processes. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis identified a module strongly correlated with freeze-resistance (r = 0.75, p = 4 × 10-9) and training status (r = 0.71, p = 6 × 10-8), which also correlated with skeletal muscle mass (r = 0.57, p = 8 × 10-5). This module was enriched for processes including extracellular matrix organization, muscle development, carbohydrate metabolism, and antioxidant activity. These molecular patterns may reflect the downstream effects of comprehensive training that integrates physical conditioning, operational experience, and psychological preparation. This study provides the first proteomic characterization of freeze-like response resistance under realistic threat conditions, supporting the view that resilience involves stable physiological adaptations rather than solely reactive stress mechanisms.

title: Isolation and characterization of rabbit intramuscular preadipocytes: Establishing a foundation for studies of intramuscular fat metabolism.
authors: Ahamba IS, Song G, Kinkpe L, Duan Q, Goswami N, Jin Z, Wu J, Dong X
abstract: Intramuscular fat (IMF) significantly influences meat quality, affecting flavor, tenderness, and juiciness. Despite extensive research on livestock such as cattle and pigs, the regulation of IMF in rabbits remains poorly understood. This study establishes a standardized in vitro method for isolating and characterizing intramuscular preadipocytes from the longissimus dorsi muscle of 3-day-old Hycole rabbits using enzymatic digestion and differential centrifugation. Three-day-old neonates were selected for initial protocol development due to their higher progenitor cell abundance and tissue accessibility, which facilitates method optimization and ensures consistent cell yields. Isolated cells displayed typical preadipocyte morphology and expressed key markers, including PREF-1, PPARγ, and Leptin, confirmed by RT-qPCR and immunofluorescence. Upon adipogenic induction, cells exhibited progressive lipid accumulation, as indicated by Oil Red O staining, and showed upregulated expression of PPARG, C/EBPa, and FABP4, confirming their differentiation potential. This study establishes a comprehensive protocol for isolating rabbit intramuscular preadipocytes, providing a foundational tool for investigating the molecular mechanisms of adipogenesis in lagomorphs. The model supports future studies on genetic and nutritional strategies to enhance rabbit meat quality while preserving its lean characteristics.

title: Disrupting the cholesterol-mechanics axis enables ferroptosis and deep drug delivery in hepatocellular carcinoma.
authors: Zhu J, Zhong Y, Yan S, Zeng X
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) develops within a fibrotic and stiffened microenvironment that limits drug penetration and suppresses regulated cell death, contributing to therapeutic resistance. Here we identify cholesterol as a central regulator linking extracellular matrix (ECM) mechanics to ferroptosis resistance through lipid raft‒mediated mechanotransduction. Spatial transcriptomics of human HCC specimens reveals enrichment of PTK2 (focal adhesion kinase, FAK) and cholesterol-associated pathways at tumor-stroma interfaces, implicating a cholesterol-mechanics axis in tumor progression. To target this vulnerability, we engineer a one-dimensional Fe-Mn oxyhydroxide nanozyme integrated with cholesterol oxidase (FeMnOOH/C). This platform simultaneously depletes cholesterol, disrupts lipid raft signaling, and remodels ECM stiffness, while amplifying ferroptosis through multienzymatic redox catalysis. FeMnOOH/C enhances membrane fluidity, promotes deep tumor penetration, and enables efficient intratumoral delivery of therapeutics. In vivo, FeMnOOH/C induces robust ferroptosis and immunogenic cell death, leading to increased cytotoxic T cell infiltration and marked tumor suppression. These findings establish mechano-metabolic reprogramming (mechanical regulation and cholesterol deprivation) as a strategy to overcome ferroptosis resistance and provide proof-of-concept support for a strategy of targeting fibrotic tumors.

title: Coacervate protocells-mediated mitochondrial transplantation restores gut epithelial energetic homeostasis in ulcerative colitis.
authors: Ding B, Chen Y, Jia Y, Li J, Tan Z, Wu W, Ouyang S, Tong B
abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is closely linked to mitochondrial dysfunction in intestinal epithelial cells, yet current therapies fail to correct underlying energy metabolism defects. While exogenous mitochondrial transplantation offers a promising strategy, its clinical translation is hindered by rapid loss of mitochondrial bioactivity ex vivo, poor delivery efficiency, and lysosomal degradation following cellular uptake. Here, we developed a biomimetic coacervate-based protocell system (HTP) via liquid-liquid phase separation of polyethylene glycol, tannic acid, and sodium hyaluronate for efficient encapsulation and delivery of functional mitochondria (HTP@Mito). HTP protocells preserved mitochondrial membrane potential and ATP synthesis capacity for up to 72 h in HBSS buffer at 37°C, far exceeding the viability of free mitochondria. Notably, HTP markedly enhanced intracellular delivery of isolated mitochondria via lipid-raft-mediated endocytosis. In a dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced murine UC model, rectally administrating HTP@Mito achieved superior therapeutic efficacy via restoring ATP levels and mitochondrial membrane potential, scavenging reactive oxygen species (ROS). Furthermore, by reducing oxidative stress, HTP@Mito rescued lysosomal function and restored impaired autophagic flux, thereby promoting mitophagy to clear damaged mitochondria. HTP@Mito treatment also repaired intestinal epithelial tight junctions, restored goblet cell-derived mucus secretion, and rebalanced gut microbiota by increasing beneficial Lachnospiraceae while reducing pathogenic Escherichia-Shigella. Collectively, this work established a versatile, biomimetic organelle delivery platform that could correct mitochondrial energy deficiency in the intestinal epithelium, providing a framework for mitochondrial transplantation in ulcerative colitis.

title: Heterojunction nanozyme achieve highly efficient antibacterial by cuproptosis-like death and ferroptosis-like death.
authors: Wang W, Zhu R, Gui H, Jin X, Wei X, Wang X
abstract: Metal-ion-mediated lethal pathways offers a highly potent strategy for antibacterial treatments. However, relying on single-pathway mechanisms often fails to overwhelm bacterial antioxidant defenses, reducing antibacterial efficacy. This study designed a heterojunction nanozyme (Cu2O/Fe2O3) that induces ferroptosis-like death and copper-mediated metabolic toxicity exhibiting cuproptosis-like features, achieving highly effective antibacterial treatment. Computational chemistry analysis indicates that the Cu2O/Fe2O3 heterointerface establishes a built-in electric field through spontaneous interfacial electron transfer, thereby enhancing its peroxidase (POD)-like activity. Within the acidic bacterial microenvironment, Cu2O/Fe2O3 catalyzes the generation of large amounts of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and releases metal ions, inducing and amplifying ferroptosis-like death, which disrupts the function of ETC enzymes by attacking iron-sulfur clusters. Concurrently, copper ions disrupt the redox balance by depleting bacillithiol (BSH), indirectly increasing bacterial susceptibility and promoting ferroptosis-like death. Furthermore, the accumulation of copper ions triggers severe metabolic impairments that biochemically resemble the cuproptosis cascade, which disrupts key enzymes of the TCA cycle and impairs the synthesis of electron donors (NADH and FADH2), thereby cutting off the supply of substrates to ETC at the upstream stage. Overall, this study demonstrates that triggering bimetallic ion-mediated metabolic disruptions induces an energy crisis in bacteria, providing a reference for multimodal antibacterial strategies.

title: Thermosensitive and tumor-targeted asparaginase fusion protein enables metabolic-immunotherapy for solid tumors.
authors: Gong L, Wang X, Zheng Y, Liu S, Zhang F, Sun Y, Qi Y, Han L
abstract: Metabolic therapies targeting tumor amino acid dependence, represented by asparaginase (ASNase), have shown limited efficacy in solid tumors, owing to poor stability, low penetration, and high immunogenicity. Here, we design a thermosensitive tumor-targeted ASNase fusion protein (ASNase-ELP-LHRH) via AlphaFold2, by integrating elastin-like polypeptide (ELP) and luteinizing hormone-releasing hormone (LHRH), to overcome these drawbacks. ELP drives in situ depot formation, extending half-life to ∼400 h (95-fold increase) and reducing anti-ASNase antibody levels 70-fold. LHRH mediates receptor-dependent tumor targeting and deep penetration. ASNase-ELP-LHRH achieves persistent asparagine (Asn) depletion, counteracting metabolic adaptation to induce nutrient starvation and apoptosis. Mechanistically, the construct blocks metastasis by suppressing epithelial-mesenchymal transition through downregulating Twist1 and upregulating E-cadherin, effectively inhibiting lung metastasis for 25 days in triple-negative breast cancer models. We further observed time-dependent changes in CD8+ T-cell effector-marker expression under Asn deprivation, characterized by dynamic alterations in IFN-γ and granzyme B expression. Combined with anti-PD-L1, this achieves a "dual boost" of antitumor immunity, durably inhibiting metastasis for 40 days and extending survival 1.5-fold. The modular ligand-exchangeable platform offers a generalizable strategy for protein optimization and establishes ASNase-ELP-LHRH as a promising metabolic-immunotherapeutic agent for solid tumors, bridging protein engineering, tumor metabolism and cancer immunology.
